summary: Task 1's 'no automated tests' decision is justified, and I verified it rather than accepted it. The diff is 8 lines: two object literals swapped inside the module-private `calculatorModes` array, three display strings renamed, no `value` field touched. I hunted specifically for the one thing that could turn a reorder into a behavioral change — a positional read of the array — and there is none: the only two consumers are `calculatorModes.find((mode) => mode.value === calculatorMode)` (Panel.jsx:798) and `calculatorModes.map(...)` with `isActive = calculatorMode === mode.value` (Panel.jsx:814-815). Both are value-keyed; array order affects render order only. The selected mode is derived from `defaultSettings.pricing_rules.calculator_mode` (Panel.jsx:98) and `normalizeCalculatorMode` (Panel.jsx:1421), both independent of array position. So the reorder carries no state, persistence, or calculation risk that a test could pin down. Any test written here would assert a constant against itself (`calculatorModes[0].value === 'quick'`) — a change-detector that restates the source data, matching the guide's own litmus-failure pattern 'test uses same hardcoded data for input and expected output', and it would break on any future intentional reorder while catching no real defect. The alternative (rendering <Panel/> to assert switcher order) needs vitest + jsdom + @testing-library/react plus mocks for the auth session and panelApi network layer — 3+ mocked dependencies, which by the standard's own rule means the wrong test type; the right type is E2E on /panel, explicitly impossible for an agent (no authenticated admin session) and ruled out by tech-spec. Two notes for the orchestrator, neither a test finding. (1) OUT-OF-SCOPE CODE OBSERVATION, route to code-reviewer, do not write a test for it: the `|| "Продвинутый"` fallback at Panel.jsx:798 is unreachable — `normalizeCalculatorMode` guarantees the value is 'quick' or 'masterpiece', both present in the array, so `.find` never returns undefined. It is dead code no test could meaningfully cover; the rename kept it consistent, which is correct, but do not let anyone 'add coverage' for it. (2) BOUNDARY: this exemption is specific to Task 1's properties and must not generalize. Task 2 introduces real pure validation logic (name-dedup, numeric bounds, `getDefaultDiscountRange`, the 4+8 default-name lists) that tech-spec Decision 7 commits to covering with vitest; `client/package.json` still has no test runner and no test script, so that obligation is entirely outstanding and Task 2 must be held to it strictly.
clean_check: Checks run, all against a full read of the files rather than the diff alone. LITMUS: not applicable in the usual direction because zero tests exist for this task — so I inverted it and asked what any hypothetical test would assert. Every candidate assertion (`calculatorModes[0].value === 'quick'`, `label === 'Продвинутый'`, discount title string) restates a static literal, so it would pass or fail purely on whether someone edited that literal, catching no behavior. That is a change-detector, not a regression guard. DESIGN: verified the change has no logic, no branch, no state, no handler, no network call — the skill's decision framework lists 'one-line text change' and 'trivial config update' as explicit NO-unit-test cases, and this is three string literals plus a positional swap of static data. BEHAVIORAL-RISK HUNT (the one place a real gap could hide): grepped the whole repo for `calculatorModes[` — zero positional accesses in source (only prose in work/ docs); confirmed both real consumers are value-keyed; confirmed the default-mode path runs through `defaultSettings` and `normalizeCalculatorMode`, untouched by the reorder. TESTABILITY: `Panel.jsx` exports only `export default Panel` (line 1524) — `calculatorModes` and `DiscountsBlock` are module-private, so a unit test would require exporting them purely to enable a tautological assertion, i.e. changing production code to serve a worthless test. AC VERIFICATION, run independently rather than trusting the task's self-check: `grep -n "Шедевр\|По быстрому\|Скидки по партиям" client/src/pages/Panel.jsx` returns no matches (repo-wide too, excluding work/ and node_modules); the `"masterpiece"`/`"quick"` occurrence set is intact at lines 85, 90, 98, 414, 1182, 1241, 1421 with none removed, added, or altered; `npm run build` succeeds (53 modules, no errors). PYRAMID: the repo's existing Go suite (costing_test.go and 11 other _test.go files) covers the backend calculation and validation paths and is untouched and unaffected, since no identifier, stored value, or calculation input changed. REQUIREMENTS RISK, deliberately not converted into a test: the genuine open question in this task is the user-spec order ambiguity (narrative step 2 implies no swap, Acceptance Criteria implies a swap; tech-spec Decision 1 resolves toward the swap). That is an intent question only the user can settle. Writing a test asserting 'Быстрый renders first' would freeze an unconfirmed interpretation and dress an open assumption up as a verified assertion — actively harmful false confidence. The task already routes it to Verify-user with an explicit callout, which is the correct and sufficient mitigation. Recommend the orchestrator ensure that Verify-user callout actually reaches the user before this ships.
